precepts.text: Moses could not cross over, but was told to charge Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people. Your job is to encourage and strengthen the men around you.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Moses prayed, “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon. But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me”. He was told, “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter”, and to go up to the top of Pisgah and behold the land with his eyes, “for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

Moses could not cross over, but look at what he was charged to do: “But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.” Charge him, encourage him, strengthen him.

That is your job as a leader: to encourage and strengthen the men around you. A leader transfers his belief onto the next man, so that the one coming after him can lead the people into what he himself was given to see. That is part of the faith that those who have the rule over you pass on.

precepts.text: The Most High divided the isles of the Gentiles, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations; the nations were never the same, he divided them by tongue and land.
precepts.point: Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
“For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron”, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds. That shows how tall and big this man was. To know who Og was, go to Genesis 10, where the nations are laid out: “By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.”

The Most High divided the isles of the Gentiles, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations. The nations were never the same; he divided them by tongue and by land. That is why the lineage of Og and the Amorites can be traced: each nation has its own family and its own place in Genesis 10.

precepts.text: The sons of Ham: Cush is Ethiopia, Mizraim is Egypt, with Phut and Canaan; Ham, the youngest son of Noah, is the progenitor of these dark nations, and Kemet and Ham mean the same thing.
precepts.point: Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
“And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.” Cush is Ethiopia, Mizraim is Egypt, with Phut and Canaan. Ham, the youngest son of Noah, is the progenitor of these dark nations; Kemet and Ham mean the same thing.

This is the family Og king of Bashan comes out of. Og was an Amorite, and the Amorites come from Canaan, the son of Ham. The Hamitic nations were known for great stature: Goliath the Philistine stood nine feet nine inches, and to this day the tallest peoples on earth, the Watusi, the Dinka and the Nilotic tribes of Sudan, Ethiopia and Kenya, are Hamites. A bedstead of iron nine cubits long fits the remnant of giants that came from Ham.

precepts.text: The Jebusite and the Amorite are of the lineage of Canaan; the Amorites are a Hamitic tribe, so Og the Amorite descends from Ham.
precepts.point: Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
The sons of Canaan: “And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite”. The Amorite is of the lineage of Canaan, the son of Ham. So the Amorites are a Hamitic tribe, and Og king of Bashan, an Amorite and the last of the remnant of giants, descends from Ham. That lineage explains the giant, for the Hamitic nations were known for great stature.

It also explains the land. Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines. The land Israel took from the two kings of the Amorites, “from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon”, all Gilead and all Bashan, was the land of the sons of Ham.

precepts.text: The Most High held Moses by him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times and the end; that is the greatness and the mighty hand Moses praised.
precepts.point: He was shown the secrets of the times, the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and the end itself; all of that stands behind this thanksgiving in Deuteronomy.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
Moses besought the Most High: “O Lord God, thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness, and thy mighty hand: for what God is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy works, and according to thy might?” The greatness shown to Moses was more than the exodus. Ezra tells what else it was: “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season”.

On that mount, held by the Most High a long season, Moses received the ten commandments and the six hundred plus commandments, ceremonial, civil, moral, dietary and sacrificial, that the Most High ordained Israel to keep. And more: he “told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying, These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” The wondrous things are the prophecies, such as Deuteronomy 28: that the people would go into slave ships under yokes of iron, lose their nationality, become a byword and an astonishment, and that a small remnant would wake up in the end days and come back. The secrets of the times are the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and he was shown the end itself.

All of that stands behind this thanksgiving. When Moses asks what God is there in heaven or in earth that can do according to thy works, he speaks as a man who has been shown the law, the prophecies and the end.

precepts.text: Moses smote the rock twice and the water came out abundantly, but because he believed not, to sanctify the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, he and Aaron would not bring the congregation into the land.
precepts.point: The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel. And the answer was final, let it suffice thee, speak no more unto me of this matter, as a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
“I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan”. The Most High had already told Moses he would not see the promised land, and here Moses is trying to get him to repent of the word he had given. The sentence came at the water of Meribah: “And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock? And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly”.

Must we fetch you water: Moses took the credit and became high minded, instead of sanctifying the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel. So the word came: “Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.” The contrast is Deuteronomy 3:3: after the war with Og the people said the Lord our God delivered them into our hands. That is sanctifying the Most High. Moses at the rock did the opposite.

“But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes”: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel, the rebels who provoked him at the rock. And the answer was final: “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.” As a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again, the Most High closed it.

points: Always remember, the battle is the Lord's; this fight is spiritual. Israel does not need weapons of mass destruction: the Bible is the weapon, and when Israel keeps the commandments the Most High fights for his people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Bashan is about to be conquered, and Og the king of Bashan came out with all his people to battle at Edrei. The Most High said fear him not, for I will deliver him and all his people and his land into thy hand, as was done to Sihon king of the Amorites at Heshbon.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: The Lord our God delivered into our hands also the king of Bashan: they were out there doing physical war, but they gave the praise, the glory, and the victory to the Most High. They did not boast in their own swords; that is how you sanctify the Most High.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Threescore cities were taken, all fenced with high walls, gates, and bars, beside unwalled towns a great many, and not one city was left untaken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: They utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city, as they did unto Sihon king of Heshbon. That command came from the Most High himself; this is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of the Bible, not the invented gospel that says he loves everybody no matter what.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Only the cattle and the spoil of the cities were taken for a prey; those were needed and were spared.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Israel took the land from the two kings of the Amorites on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon.
Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His bedstead was a bedstead of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds, showing how tall and big this man was.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: The conquered land was divided: from Aroer by the river Arnon and half mount Gilead to the Reubenites and the Gadites, and the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half tribe of Manasseh.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: All the region of Argob with all Bashan was called the land of giants, because the giants there were of Og's kin, of his family.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob and called it after his own name, Bashan-havoth-jair, unto this day.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: All that were meet for the war were to pass over armed before their brethren, while the wives, the little ones, and the much cattle abode in the cities already given, until the Most High gave rest to their brethren and they also possessed their land beyond Jordan.

When you read these wars, put yourself in the position of the brothers going out. Being promised victory over the land did not mean every man would survive it; Israel still had casualties, and there were brothers that gave their lives for their people.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Joshua was commanded at that time: thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings; so shall he do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest.
Ye shall not fear them, for the Lord your God he shall fight for you; the victories over Sihon and Og were the proof set before Joshua's own eyes.

The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel. And the answer was final, let it suffice thee, speak no more unto me of this matter, as a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Get thee up into the top of Pisgah and behold the land with thine eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, for thou shalt not go over this Jordan; seeing it from the mountain was all that was granted.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people and cause them to inherit the land. The Most High said plainly whom he would deal with for the crossing.
Promotion comes from the Most High: he was dealing with Moses and declared who he wanted in charge, and Moses was to strengthen the man chosen to replace him.
